title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Standards Manual — Night Edition. Keep it, take a challenger, re-roll for a fresh hand, or play the category standard straight.

options.label: Standards Manual — Night Edition
options.lineage: identity standards manuals (Unimark, NASA '75) · night edition
options.thesis: The whole site is Ejaz's practice manual: numbered spec plates on matte black stock, white ink, one signal-yellow spot color.
options.viewport: Plate 00: a masthead name-plate — EJAZ ALI set large in expanded grotesque, the tagline as a specimen line beneath, plate number and revision stamp in mono at the corners.
options.risk: Executed timidly it collapses into 'minimal dark portfolio'; the numbering, rules, and stamp details must carry real information or the manual is cosplay.

options.label: Color-Field Glass Partition
options.case: Fuses cleanly: one pane one statement, backlit panes for state — strong agency-office identification, loses the plate-numbering grammar.
options.thesis: The page is a black-glazed partition wall: every section a pane of glass, most clear, a few saturated fields lighting up for what matters now.
options.viewport: A wall elevation: thin black mullions dividing the first screen into rectilinear panes; the name sits inside one clear pane, the tagline in another, one cobalt pane holds the primary action.
options.risk: Glass metaphors drift into generic 'card grid with better borders' if pane sizes and the single lit note aren't ruthless.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom
options.case: Beautiful narrative fit — work emerges into light, stations map to shape→build→ship — but the amber monochrome and moody pace trade 'clean agency' for art project.
options.thesis: The practice as a darkroom: projects move compose → expose → develop → fix → wash → dry, and case studies literally emerge on the page.
options.viewport: Under amber wash: station names as grease-pencil labels down the left, one print mid-development center frame, timer digits ticking in mono.
options.risk: One-hue amber across a full persuade page can tire the eye; B2B founders may read art piece before vendor.

options.label: Live ASCII Scene
options.case: Fuses poorly: glyph texture fights the 'very clean' mandate and B2B legibility; wins novelty, loses the founder's five-second read.
options.thesis: The hero is a live character-grid rendering — a business dashboard dissolving from manual chaos into running software, drawn in one mono alphabet.
options.viewport: A 40×24-ish character field animating a before/after workflow in green phosphor, name and tagline as selectable text inside the same grid.
options.risk: Developer-toy energy: recruiters smile, cautious founders bounce.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every developer portfolio ships: near-black ground, one neon accent, gradient headline, pill nav, glowing project cards.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline with a soft glow, subhead, two buttons, a marquee of tech logos below.
canonCard.risk: Memorable for an hour, indistinguishable by lunch — exactly the template feeling you named as failure.
